p.title: Scarcity: ₹1,000 for the month
p.challenge: Your wants add up to more than ₹1,000. That's scarcity! Choose: plan every rupee and save at least 10%
A farm can grow 6 tonnes of wheat (y) OR 3 tonnes of cotton (x). Make this production possibility line pass through (0, 6) and (3, 0)
p.winText: Slope −2: each extra tonne of cotton means giving up 2 tonnes of wheat. That is the opportunity cost!

p.title: Who solves the central problems?
p.challenge: Which kind of economy is India? Answer the questions to find out

nodes.text: What, how and for whom to produce?
nodes.info: Every economy faces these three central problems because of scarcity.

nodes.text: Decided only by buyers and sellers through prices?

nodes.info: Also called a centrally planned economy: the government decides.
India uses both markets and government.

p.challenge: Kulfi demand schedule: ₹10 → 50, ₹20 → 40, ₹30 → 30, ₹40 → 20. With x = price (₹10s) and y = kulfis (tens), make the demand curve pass through all 4 points
p.winText: The demand curve slopes downward: as the price rises, quantity demanded falls. That is the law of demand!

p.title: Is this message a fraud?
p.challenge: You get a message: 'You won ₹5,000! Enter your UPI PIN to receive it.' Follow the flow and stay safe

nodes.text: Do you need a UPI PIN to receive money?
Wrong! The PIN sends money OUT
nodes.info: You never need a UPI PIN to receive money. Report such frauds on helpline 1930.
Banks never ask for your PIN, OTP, CVV or passwords. Offers to double money quickly are also likely frauds.

p.title: From idea to startup
p.challenge: Arrange the 7 steps of building a startup, from problem to funding

nodes.text: Spot a real problem people face
Market research: talk to possible customers
Build a simple first version (prototype / MVP)
Test it with users and take feedback

nodes.info: Change the product or the target customers, then build, test and take feedback again.
Product, customers, costs, price and expected profit.
Own savings (bootstrapping), family, bank loans, angel investors or venture capital. Investors usually get equity.

p.title: Patent, trademark or copyright?
p.challenge: Your team made a clay fridge that runs without electricity. Sort each thing by the law that protects it.

items.why: A patent protects a new invention, for 20 years in India.

items.text: A new kind of solar water pump
items.why: A new invention is protected by a patent.

items.text: The brand name printed on the fridge
items.why: A trademark protects a brand name or logo.
A trademark protects a brand name or logo.
Copyright protects creative work such as books.
Copyright protects creative work such as music.
Copyright protects creative work such as software.
